tasks.short: Monitor supplier delivery, quality, service and spending, and agree corrective action.

steps.what: Collect supplier commitments, delivery results and spending records.
Reconcile supplier results against service targets and budget.
Read supplier explanations and departmental reports about service failures.

loop.input: Supplier explanations and service incident reports linked to a supplier scorecard.
loop.output: Source-linked issues, disputed claims and missing evidence.
loop.check: Require source passages; validate identifiers and figures against the scorecard. Treat explanations as claims.
loop.stop: One extraction and one validation retry per report; route unsupported claims to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explanations vary in wording and structure; numeric thresholds cannot interpret them.

steps.what: Review operational impact and alternatives with department managers.
Discuss causes, recovery commitments and commercial remedies with the supplier.
Approve corrective action and any changes to spending or supplier commitments.
Record agreed actions, assign owners and chase due dates.

tasks.design: Join commitments from the {PROCUREMENT}, receipts from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and spending from the {ERP} into a supplier dashboard in the {BI}. A bounded reader prepares source-linked issue briefs, while the {WORKFLOW} records approved actions and sends internal reminders. People handle supplier discussions and approve changes to commitments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier identifiers, receipt dates and service definitions differ across records. Reconciling them costs more than building the chart.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and scheduled joins can support scorecards. AI-assisted coding reduces implementation effort, and bounded extraction can shorten report reading.
tasks.still_hard: Attributing failures, measuring service quality and negotiating remedies remain difficult, especially with disputed evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether poor results reflect supplier failure, internal disruption or an unrealistic contract, and preserve negotiating options.

ambition.what: Weekly recovery decisions for suppliers showing deteriorating service.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time reconciling reports and more time resolving service risks. Contract and spending authority still follows existing delegation limits.

reach.task: Assess critical supplier concentration and continuity exposure.
reach.learn: Combine operational dependency, switching time and financial exposure into investment choices.

evidence.claim: Report summaries and dashboard questions are available capabilities; reliable results require prepared data models.
Deterministic joins, scorecards and action reminders are a plausible supplier-monitoring design, not a documented deployment here.

assumptions: This describes recurring oversight through procurement and department managers, rather than daily purchasing.
The time split gives substantial weight to discussion and judgement; collection effort varies by supplier.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for one supplier segment using existing infrastructure.
unknowns: Whether supplier identifiers match across the available systems.
Which service measures, budgets and remedies are contractually agreed.
Available access, export rights and approval limits.
Whether personal data in incident reports requires additional access restrictions.
research_questions: Which measures predict disruption early enough to change an operational decision?
Can standard reporting and reminder configuration cover the first release?
new_work: Resolve unmatched suppliers and disputed receipts.
Review extracted claims against source reports.
Maintain service definitions, thresholds and integration mappings.
Check stale feeds and close completed supplier actions.

tasks.short: Coordinate inbound, internal and outbound goods flows through supervisors, resolving capacity and service trade-offs.

steps.what: Review expected receipts, stock, production requirements and dispatch commitments.
Confirm actual constraints with production, warehouse and transport supervisors.
Compare feasible movement plans and their service, cost and sustainability effects.
Choose priorities and approve changes to movement plans.
Update movement schedules and issue instructions to warehouse and production teams.
Agree changed delivery or collection arrangements with carriers and suppliers.
Check execution and escalate unresolved delays or unsafe conditions.

tasks.design: Configure exception views in the {OPS_SYSTEM} and add a deterministic scenario calculator where existing planning functions fall short. The {WORKFLOW} transfers approved movement plans into schedules and internal instructions, with version and capacity checks. Managers and supervisors confirm physical constraints and direct interventions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recorded stock and capacity often lag physical conditions. Local constraints and external transport commitments are difficult to represent consistently.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing operational events, configurable alerts and conventional constraint calculations can improve preparation without a model loop.
tasks.still_hard: Unrecorded congestion, damaged goods, equipment failures and safety judgements require people close to the operation.
tasks.human_edge: Balance production continuity, customer promises, safety and practical site knowledge when no option satisfies every constraint.

ambition.what: Same-shift recovery decisions for emerging bottlenecks.

tasks.altitude: The manager receives earlier exception signals and compares feasible responses faster. Supervisors retain physical execution and safety authority; no new personnel decision rights are implied.

reach.learn: Translate recurring bottlenecks into capital needs, resilience benefits and investment payback.

evidence.claim: Operational alerts, constraint calculations and approved schedule updates can use deterministic technology.
The digest provides no documented case establishing automated physical goods-flow management for this setting.

assumptions: This supplemental task applies to a company operating production or distribution facilities.
The manager coordinates through supervisors rather than routinely dispatching individual workers.
The workflow id 'other' denotes physical goods flow, which has no dedicated id in the supplied list.
The design changes goods schedules, not machinery controls or individual staff allocation.
Build ranges cover one site; access and consultation include national rules where changes affect working arrangements.
unknowns: Which operational planning, alerting and schedule-update features are already licensed.
Accuracy and latency of stock, capacity and equipment records.
Which movement changes require transport, safety or spending approval.
Applicable national consultation requirements and employee-representation arrangements.
Availability of reliable transport and emissions factors.
research_questions: Which constraints explain most failed movement plans?
Can existing planning configuration produce useful options before custom calculations are needed?
How should proposed schedules be tested against actual site conditions before rollout?
new_work: Maintain capacity constraints and transport factors.
Investigate stale operational events and false alerts.
Check approved plan versions before schedule updates.
Review recurring overrides with site supervisors.

tasks.short: Set prices and business customer credit terms using demand forecasts, costs, payment history and commercial judgement.

steps.what: Gather demand forecasts, costs, sales results and customer payment history.
Calculate margin, volume and cash effects under alternative prices and credit terms.
Discuss demand assumptions, customer context and exposure with finance and sales managers.
Approve prices within delegated margin and discount limits.
Approve credit limits and payment terms within financial delegation.
Enter approved prices and terms with their scope and effective dates.

tasks.design: Join the {ERP} and {CRM} data on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, then calculate versioned margin, demand and cash scenarios for a {BI} view. Configure approvals in the {WORKFLOW} and transfer approved prices and credit terms into the {ERP} and {CRM}, checking scope, effective dates and delegation limits. The first version needs no model loop.
tasks.previous_blocker: Costs, customer terms and forecasts use different definitions and update cycles. Approval decisions often arrive separately from the records that implement them.
tasks.enabler_now: Conventional scenario calculations, versioned datasets and existing approval functions can connect analysis to controlled record updates.
tasks.still_hard: Demand response is uncertain, payment history can mislead, and commercial exceptions may matter more than the calculated optimum.
tasks.human_edge: Choose acceptable margin and credit exposure while judging customer relationships, competitive response and uncertainty.

ambition.what: Weekly price reviews for product groups with rapidly changing input costs.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time rebuilding scenarios and can revisit pricing assumptions sooner. Pricing authority stays within delegation, and finance retains credit approval.

reach.task: Set portfolio margin and working-capital priorities.
reach.learn: Assess price elasticity, cash conversion and concentration risk across business lines.

evidence.claim: Planning software can produce reports and flag anomalies; this supports analysis rather than autonomous commercial approval.
Deterministic scenario calculations and controlled updates are a plausible first implementation for this task.
GDPR Article 22 limits certain solely automated decisions concerning individuals.
The AI Act lists AI systems used to evaluate natural-person creditworthiness among high-risk uses.

assumptions: The initial scope is business customer accounts; natural-person credit scoring is excluded.
Pricing and credit approvals are separate and follow existing delegation.
Forecast scenarios expose uncertainty rather than claiming a known causal demand response.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for one business line with existing systems.
unknowns: Actual pricing and credit decision rights.
Whether accounts include sole traders or other natural persons.
Availability of historical price changes, lost sales and comparable demand observations.
Existing approval configuration and write access to commercial records.
Treatment of negotiated contracts, taxes, currencies and retrospective changes.
research_questions: Which demand assumptions can be tested against historical price changes?
Can existing commercial rules and approval configuration cover record activation?
Would any proposed expansion introduce natural-person decisions requiring additional GDPR and EU AI Act assessment?
new_work: Maintain cost definitions, approval limits and scenario assumptions.
Investigate missing prices, conflicting terms and stale forecasts.
Compare realised margin and payment outcomes with approved assumptions.
Review rejected updates and verify effective dates.

tasks.short: Help customers and support shelf replenishment and inventory checks during occasional sales-floor work.

steps.what: Greet customers and establish what help they need.
Look up product details, availability and stock location when needed.
Explain options, locate goods and help the customer choose.
Move available goods to shelves and check presentation.
Count goods at selected shelf and storage locations.
Enter counts and flag discrepancies for inventory review.

tasks.design: Configure a mobile lookup and count screen in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, using product information from the {ECOMMERCE} where needed. Capture counts once, calculate discrepancies and route them through the {WORKFLOW} to the inventory controller. Customer assistance, physical counting and replenishment remain human work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shared terminals interrupt customer conversations, and physical counts may need separate entry. Much of the task involves physical action that software cannot remove.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing mobile screens and barcode capture can reduce lookup and recording effort. A small integration may connect product details without requiring a model.
tasks.still_hard: Misplaced goods, inaccurate stock records, customer needs and shelf presentation require observation and physical action.
tasks.human_edge: Read customer cues, explain choices clearly and notice operational problems during direct floor contact.
tasks.altitude: The manager gains a little uninterrupted floor time through faster lookup and count capture. The role and decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Evaluate service standards through direct customer observation.
reach.learn: Turn repeated floor observations into service priorities while distinguishing patterns from isolated anecdotes.

evidence.claim: Mobile product lookup, barcode count capture and discrepancy routing are established deterministic patterns.
The digest supplies no documented case showing that software replaces the physical or interpersonal work described here.

assumptions: This supplemental task applies to retail or customer-facing sites.
A general manager covers busy periods or observes operations; routine floor supervision belongs to site supervisors.
The workflow covers related floor activities, not a mandatory sequence for every customer.
Count records are observations; stock adjustments require the inventory controller's separate approval.
Build ranges assume existing mobile-compatible systems and devices; national consultation applies if working arrangements change.
unknowns: Whether existing devices and licences already support lookup and count capture.
Whether product information and store stock are consistently linked.
Frequency and duration of the manager's actual floor work.
Inventory adjustment approval rules and applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Does lookup delay or inaccurate stock cause more customer interruption?
Can existing mobile configuration remove duplicate count entry without custom development?
new_work: Resolve synchronisation failures and duplicate counts.
Review discrepancies before authorising stock adjustments.
Keep mobile screens and shared-device access usable.

role.altitude: The manager's week shifts modestly from collecting and reconciling information toward supplier recovery, commercial trade-offs and operational interventions. Physical work and consequential judgement remain substantial; existing financial, safety and personnel delegations still apply.
reach: Support the chief executive's supplier-continuity decisions with evidence of dependency and switching time.
Support capacity investment decisions with recurring bottleneck and service-impact analysis.
Connect pricing decisions to portfolio margin and working-capital priorities.
skills_to_grow: Define operational measures and recognise unreliable data.
Evaluate integration exceptions and approval controls.
Translate operational evidence into investment choices.
role.ambitious_version: Run a weekly cross-functional review that makes explicit choices about supplier recovery, bottleneck capacity and changing margins, then checks whether those choices improved service and cash outcomes.
